dendry-noise.look: The best river tree in the family on the sheet. Close view: irregular connected rivers with fine twig tributaries, thicker in the low regions, no axis in the FFT. It reads as a river map rather than frost or spokes. The 4x wide panel still shows branching everywhere, with regional zones where rivers are thicker because width follows the control height. A few hubs where several rivers meet remain and occasional crossings form small closed diamonds. The relief carve is softer than catchment-rivers: smooth valleys following the terrain, with less fine dissection. At 77 cells across 512 px it dissolves into dendritic texture; no single river spans that view. 3D is level 0 only: a network of straight rods joined at junctions, the slice shows clusters of ellipses. The 3x3 window thumb and the paper-style 5x5 window thumb are near identical.
dendry-noise.dims: 2D measured, 1-4 levels. 3D measured, level 0 only (5x5x5 control, 3x3x3 segments, lowest of 26 neighbours). 4D not written: 5^4 = 625 control evals.
dendry-noise.range: Mask [-1,1], saturating. Carve test output not normalised, min -1.106, max 0.938 at these params.
dendry-noise.artifacts: c0ratio 3.01 is the lab probe saturating on thin lines. The bisecting jump scanner found 0 true jumps on mask, proximity and carve (worst 0.007). Scalar 2740 ns at 4 levels, 2338 at 3, 1457 at 1, 7505 with 2-Perlin control and 5x5 level 0. Width is a control-height proxy, not discharge. Hubs reduced, not gone. By eye the longest rivers are about 10-20 cells. Far above the 5x Perlin guideline: a hero or bake node.
dendry-noise.node_shape: DendryNoise: Feature Scale, Levels (1-4), Epsilon, Tributary Skew, Width, Width Ratio, Width Growth, Stochastic Descent, Control (hash-only default, optional Source at higher cost), Control Scale, Output {Mask, Proximity, Carve}, Valley Profile {V, U, Box}. Levels=1 plus profiles covers basin-tree.
dendry-noise.port_notes: Written from the idea entry's method description; neither the paper nor the GPL code was fetched. Window: 3x3 segments per level, 5x5 control, child searches the 2x2 parent cells on its side, parent level only (scalar 2740 ns vs 9582 ns for paper-style, near-identical look). Drop links longer than link*size rather than shrinking them (shrink gave 4 true jumps, worst 0.89; drop gave 0). Cap each level's radius at (1 + (1-eps)/2 - link)*size, level 0 at (1-eps)/2. That cap limits carved valleys to 0.2 cells, so Carve needs a 5x5 level 0 (lite=2, 7x7 control). Stochastic descent: one hash mask per cell picks eligible neighbours, falling back to all if none is lower; links are strictly downhill, so no cycles.

critic.notes: Seeds 7 and 42 confirm the close view: a connected irregular tree with twig tributaries, no axis in the FFT, no seams. It is the only entry that reads as a river map, and nothing in the existing nodes sheet gives a connected tree (Ridged and warped F2-F1 give webs whose lines cross). Baseline flaw the prototyper understated: at 96 cells across (seed 42, window 24) the width proxy follows the drift field, so half the frame is a white blob and the other half thin scribble. Star hubs remain at several junctions at seed 7 and some crossings close small diamonds. 3D vol at seed 7 is straight rods, level 0 only; no 4D. Paper-window thumb matches the lite thumb, so the 3x3 cut-down is justified. Cost is 55x Perlin scalar: a hero or bake node for heightmaps, not a building block. Port is a fixed 5x5 control + 3x3 segments per level + 4 parent lookups, all fixed-count, but four levels of segment arrays per lane is a lot of registers.
critic.improved: Added wmode=1: level-0 width from the segment's own 3x3 min/max of the control instead of the absolute control height. The first attempt used the sample's 5x5 window min/max and seamed at every cell edge (17 true jumps); making it a per-segment property fixed that (0 jumps) at the same cost (2743 vs 2700 ns). At 96 cells the fat/thin zones are gone and the tree covers the frame evenly with local trunk/twig hierarchy; the close view is nearly unchanged. It equalises texture, it does not add real discharge hierarchy. Proto edited, previous copy at t_dendry_noise.prev.cpp.

tournament.notes: Re-ran check, speed, jump scan (seed 7) and rendered seeds 7 and 42 at windows 8 and 24 plus a vol at seed 7. Confirmed: connected irregular tree, isotropic FFT, no seams, 2700 ns scalar (54.5x Perlin). Not obtainable from existing nodes: Ridged and warped cellular give crossing webs. Flaws: star hubs and diamond crossings remain at seed 7; 3D is straight rods, level 0 only; no 4D so tiling breaks; rivers never exceed 10-20 cells. Cost makes it a hero/bake node. Port is all fixed-count windows (5x5 control, 3x3 segments per level, 4 parent lookups) but four levels of segment state per lane is heavy; AVX2 cost is unmeasured, the prototyper's 60-100 ns is an estimate I cannot confirm.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured. 2D hash-only control: 60-100 ns at 4 levels, 50-80 at 3, 25-40 at 1. 2D with 2-Perlin control and 5x5 level 0: 170-250 ns. 3D level 0: 200-300 ns. No 4D.

artist-terrain.note: Wide seed 42: connected irregular river tree with twigs, no axis. 54x Perlin, 3D rods, no 4D, hubs and diamonds remain. Bake node for river masks, not a building block.

artist-material.note: Connected, tapered river or lightning mask that no graph makes. Star hubs remain, the 3D rods are useless, and the estimated cost makes it a bake node.

voxel-engineer.note: Only true branching tree here, but the relief is soft and vol is straight rods. 60-100 ns est, unmeasured. Fine per column for a bake; no 4D. Reference code is GPL: paper only.

maintainer.note: The only true connected river tree on the sheets, isotropic, no seams. 2700 ns scalar, 60-250 ns est, no 4D. A bake/hero node, not a FastNoise building block; I would not take the support burden.

graphics-researcher.note: A real connected river tree with isotropic FFT; this is the Gaillard et al. Dendry paper, so not new, and 54x Perlin makes it a bake node. Per-segment width and stochastic descent are good additions.

creative.note: Real lightning trees with twigs, unlike any web-based stock output.

master.one_liner: Distance to an implicit hierarchical tree built on the fly from jittered multi-resolution grids, each point linked toward its lowest-control neighbour: rivers, cracks, lightning, lichen, drainage networks (Gaillard et al. I3D 2019).
master.look: Branching channel/river networks with consistent downhill topology, dry-mud and ceramic crack webs, Lichtenberg lightning, root/vein systems. No cellular variant on the sheet has connected tree topology (F2-F1 gives closed cells, not branches).
master.algorithm:
Params: Control C (GeneratorSource, e.g. low-frequency fbm = elevation), Levels L (int 1-4), Epsilon (jitter range 0..0.5), Displacement (float), Output enum {Distance, Elevation, Mask}, SlopeMin per level (floats).
Level-1 cell size s1 = 1 (Feature Scale), level l size s_l = s1/2^(l-1).
Point of cell c at level l: P_l(c) = (c + 0.5 + Epsilon*(rnd2(hash(seed,l,c))-0.5)) * s_l. Control value at a point: C(P) (a Source eval at another position; allowed).
Level 1 segments: for each coarse cell c, segment Seg1(c) = P1(c) -> P1(n*) where n* = argmin over the 3x3 neighbours n of C(P1(n)) (the lowest-elevation neighbour, 'water flows down'); if c itself is the minimum, zero-length segment (a local minimum = lake/sink). Optional displacement: bend midpoint perpendicular by Displacement*rnd (quadratic Bezier = cheap stand-in for the paper's Catmull-Rom subdivision).
Level l>1 segments: for each fine cell c at level l, its point P_l(c) connects to the nearest point on the nearest parent segment among the parent segments of the 3x3 parent cells around c (paper's 'Rivers' strategy: snap to A, B or the midpoint; 'NearestPoint' for cracks/lightning). A per-level SlopeMin raises child elevation so rivers only flow down.
Evaluation at p: for l in 1..L: for each cell c in the 3x3 window at level l: d = min(d, distToSegment(p, Seg_l(c))) (segments entirely determined by hashes + Control, so no state). Distance output: 1 - clamp(d/s1); Elevation: C(nearest segment point) + Slope*d (terrain with consistent valleys); Mask: d < Width.
Cost control: cache Control evals: level 1 needs C at the 5x5 coarse points (25 evals), level-2 connection needs only distances to already-built parent segments (no new C evals), so total Source evals = 25 regardless of L.
3D: extruded 2D (z enters the hash as a seed slice) by default; a true 3D variant with 3x3x3 windows and 125 control evals is possible but expensive.
master.why_new: Connected, hierarchical, direction-consistent branching is impossible to build from Perlin/Cellular graphs; Dendry is the only known pointwise construction for it and it directly gives terrains with rivers that actually drain downhill (the control function decides the flow).
master.simd_plan:
All loops fixed size: 49 point generations, 25 argmins (branch-free compare+Select chains), 25 segment distances (~15 ops each with Select for clamped t), level 1 adds 25x9 projections. 2D estimate: level-0 ~2700 ops (~25x Perlin, ~30 ns), two levels ~60 ns. 3D: level 0 only, 3x3x3 window with the 5x5 rule replaced by Max Distance = 0.5 cell (27 points x (hash + control) + 27 argmin over 26 + 27 segment distances ~ 10x Perlin3D). 4D: no native support (fallback drops w; tiling not supported), state clearly.
[DendryNoise, lit-recent] All loops fixed: 25 Control evals at hashed points (batch them as one 25-wide Gen call per lane set), 9 x L segment-distance evaluations with Select for the argmin and snap logic. 2D ~ 25*Control + ~150 segment ops: with a cheap Control (Perlin) ~30-40x Perlin; acceptable for a 'make the hard thing easy' node, and GeneratorCache-friendly. 3D default = extrusion (cheap), true 3D flagged as 125 evals + 27*L segments.
master.continuity: C0: min of point-segment distances is continuous; segment endpoints depend only on hashes and on Control values at fixed points, so they do not change across the sample domain. Elevation output is continuous when Slope*d is used; Mask is binary.
master.params: Control (GeneratorSource), Levels (int), Epsilon (float), Displacement (float), Strategy enum {Rivers, NearestPoint, Angle}, SlopeMin (float), Width (hybrid, Mask), Output enum.
master.risks:
Window seams: a parent segment of a cell outside the 3x3 parent window can be nearer than any inside; mitigate by clamping segment length to one cell (Epsilon<=0.5 and connection to the 3x3 only) which the paper also relies on. Cost is high; 4D and true 3D questionable. The look depends strongly on Control quality.
[DendriticNoise, terrain-tools-engines] Expensive (one of the costliest nodes); control-field-driven flow direction means features of C's scale must be larger than the lattice or the tree fragments; a Source control costs ~50-75 evals per sample; no 4D.
master.cost_note: About 30 ns at one level and 60 ns at two in 2D with a cheap control (25-50x Perlin); single-level 3D about 10x Perlin3D; no native 4D.
master.variant_notes: Multi-level Dendry and its lite forms. The reference code is GPL-3.0, so implement from the paper. Source-driven control costs tens of evals per sample.

basin-tree.look: Thin connected wiggly rivers with small blobs at some sinks, no tributaries below one cell, so it looks sparser and more skeletal than dendry-noise. With a smooth value base and no stochastic descent the wide view is star clusters, which matches the earlier judge note about starfish. The valley profiles are the real contribution: V gives dissected gullies, U gives soft troughs, Box gives flat-floored slot channels with crisp walls, all clean in hillshade and with no seams. Relief: soft valleys following the base, gentle compared to catchment-rivers. 3D vol: straight rods joined at junctions, same as dendry level 0.

basin-tree.node_shape: DendryNoise with Levels=1; Valley Profile {V, U, Box} and a ridge flag become DendryNoise members.
basin-tree.port_notes: Algorithmically dendry level 0 with a better valley output. Hash-only control removes the Source cost. R=1 costs 1236 ns scalar against 1970 ns for R=2 but limits valley width to (1-jitter)/2 cells, so R=2 is the carve setting.

critic.notes: Thin wiggly connected channels with small blobs at sinks; sparse, no sub-cell tributaries. Algorithmically it is dendry level 0, so I agree with the merge. The valley profile sweep (V, U, Box) is the real contribution: clean hillshade, no seams, and the Box profile gives slot canyons nothing else in the family makes. Those profiles should become members of the dendry node. The 3D vol is the same rod network as dendry level 0. Not re-rendered separately; dendry levels=1 covers it.

tournament.notes: Agree with the merge: it is dendry level 0. Thin wiggly connected channels, sparse, blobs at sinks, same rod network in 3D. The V/U/Box valley profile sweep is clean in hillshade with no seams and the Box slot canyons are a look nothing else here makes; those profiles belong on the dendry node. Not re-rendered separately.

master.one_liner: Dendritic valley/ridge/canyon networks carved into a base relief from a steepest-descent graph on a jittered lattice: every cell drains to its lowest neighbour, the surface is base minus the max of finite-width valley profiles around the nearby stream segments.
master.look:
Fern/antler-like branching valley systems converging into basins, with valley width and depth growing downstream; U mode gives flat-floored troughs with parabolic walls (glacial valleys), Box mode gives a slot-canyon network seen from above, Ridge mode gives dendritic mountain spines with spurs. Domain-warping the input position upstream (ordinary DomainWarp node) turns the straight segments into meandering ones and the result reads as real drainage. Prototyped: BasinV/U/Canyon/RidgeTree, BasinWarped, CanyonWarped. Good for river valleys, badlands, canyon lands, glacial troughs, cave networks in 3D.
[CellularDrainage, cell-relations] Dendritic branching: many short tributaries merging into thicker trunks that end in small lakes, like river basins, lightning, leaf veins or root systems (3D tubes). With a large-scale source as elevation, the trees follow the real downhill direction of that terrain, so rivers are consistent with an FBm heightmap. No existing node makes tree-like (acyclic, branching) structures.
master.algorithm: Lattice: jittered integer grid (CellularDistance style), one feature point c_i per cell (jitter ~0.45). Base: a cheap smooth field B evaluated at cell points (prototype used 2-octave Perlin at scale 0.15; a node should use bilinear value noise of a 4x coarser lattice = 4 hashes per cell so no source evals are needed). Downstream of cell i: d(i) = argmin over its 8 (26 in 3D) neighbours j of B(c_j), kept as i itself if none is lower (sink = lake/sea). Segments s_i = [c_i, c_d(i)] form a forest of trees that terminate at the minima of B, so there are no cycles by construction (B strictly decreases along every chain). Pointwise eval at p: for every cell i in the (2R+1)^dim window (R=2 so that any segment with an endpoint within 1 cell of p is included): t = clamp(dot(p-c_i, v)/|v|^2), d = |p - c_i - t v|, hseg = lerp(B(c_i), B(c_d), t); size = sat((h0 - hseg)*k) (lower base = larger stream, the stream-order proxy); width w = W0*(0.25+size), depth D = D0*(0.3+size); profile v = D*(1-smoothstep(0,w,d)) [V], or floor f = 0.5*w*size, e = sat((d-f)/w), v = D*(1-e^2) [U, glacial trough], or v = D*(1-smoothstep(f, f+wall, d)) [Box, slot canyon]. carve = max_i v_i. out = B(p)*relief - carve (+ optional fine fbm). ridge mode: out = -(out). Longitudinal profile is concave-up automatically because hseg follows B along the chain; per-segment hashed knickpoints (step in hseg) give waterfalls. Multi-scale: run a second, 4x finer instance whose B is this node's own output at the fine cell points (fixed extra evals) so tributaries join the trunk valleys; 2D only at sane cost.
master.why_new: Nothing in the library produces tree topology: cellular gives closed cells, ridged fractals give isotropic crinkles. A graph of existing nodes cannot express 'drain to the lowest neighbour' or 'distance to a segment'. Differs from the sibling FlowNetwork (Scheidegger lattice, one global flow direction) and QuadDendrite (quadtree parents): here streams follow a smooth base so they converge radially into basins/lakes and the stream size, valley width and floor height all derive from that base, which is what makes it read as terrain.
master.simd_plan: Window: compute B for the (2R+3)^dim block once per lane batch (7x7=49 cells in 2D, each 4 hashes + lerp; store in registers/stack arrays indexed by constant loops), then loop the 5x5 inner cells: pick downstream by 8 compare+Select, segment distance (FMA, one Sqrt or compare on squared distance with w^2), profile via smoothstep, running Max. All loops have constant trip counts; no per-lane branching. 3D: 7^3=343 base cells and 125 segments (27-neighbour argmin) = roughly 8-10x CellularDistance 3D; acceptable for a landform node, and it yields branching cave tunnels. 4D: 7^4 is prohibitive; implement with R=1 (5^4 bases, 81 segments) and document that tiling should go through GenTileable2D's 4D path only at low resolution, or decline 4D. Estimated 2D cost ~25-40x Perlin (scalar proto 310x because it re-evaluated fbm 9 times per cell; the block-caching plan removes that).
master.continuity: C0: the surface is a max of continuous profile functions over a fixed set of segments, and the base is continuous. Verified c0ratio 7.99-8.01 in all modes. Seams are impossible as long as every segment whose influence reaches p is in the window, which holds because profile width w < 1 cell and segments are at most 1 cell long (sqrt(2)+2*jitter with jitter); keep max width + jitter below 1 cell or raise R.
master.params: Feature Scale (mixin), Jitter, Base Scale (coarse lattice ratio), Relief (base amplitude kept), Depth, Width (hybrid: lets a mask thin valleys regionally), Profile enum {V, U, Box}, Wall Width (box), Size Gain (how fast width grows downstream), Ridge bool, Knickpoint Chance, Fine Detail amplitude.
master.risks:
Straight 1-cell segments look artificial without an upstream warp (cheap to add, but a user must know). Many parallel chains run into the same sink when the base is very smooth; the base lattice ratio and jitter control this. Junctions are a plain max, so tributary mouths are abrupt (a smooth max fixes it). Cost in 3D/4D. Needs a measured output normalisation (ScaleOutput) since carve depth depends on params.
[CellularDrainage, cell-relations] With hash elevations the descent runs are short (a few cells), so trees look like short dendrites, not long rivers; long rivers need a smooth Elevation source, which multiplies source cost by the 5^D hash window. Width-by-elevation is only a proxy for flow accumulation (a true Strahler order is global). Only one outgoing edge per point: no braided channels.
master.cost_note: Estimated 2D cost ~25-40x Perlin (scalar proto 310x because it re-evaluated fbm 9 times per cell; the block-caching plan removes that).
master.variant_notes: Single-level steepest descent to the lowest neighbour. CellularDrainage contributes tapered widths, lightning bias and 3D tubes.

queue.name: BasinTree
queue.reason: Steepest-descent forest with real tree topology (J3 top pick), but J2 read earlier sheets as starfish spokes and the 7x7 block costs ~40 ns. See it warped beside flow-network and fern-fold.

catchment-rivers.look: Global axis layout: long parallel gullies, not usable for this family. Local frame layout (rows = distance to a steepest-descent trunk, flow runs into that trunk, K=4): the elevation output is the most convincing terrain in the family, with sharp dissected ridges and side gullies feeding broad trunk valleys, in both hillshade and relief. In plan view the trunks are straight spokes meeting at star-shaped hubs. Stochastic descent reduces the stars but they remain. The channel mask is its weak output: thick straight trunks over a field of fine speckle and wormlike twigs. K sweep 2, 4, 8, 16 is close to indistinguishable by eye. With hash-only value control the base goes boxy at the wide view and peaks become spiky, so the terrain view uses Perlin control. 3D vol is stacked extruded sheets, not a network.
catchment-rivers.dims: 2D measured. 3D is crossfaded 2D laminae at 2x cost, continuous in z but extruded in look. The clear reason is that the walker interval property needs a 1D lateral. 4D not written.
catchment-rivers.range: Elevation-based terrain output not normalised: min -1.362, max 1.271 over 8 seeds and offsets at the listed params. A port needs Output Min/Max with a measured constant.
catchment-rivers.artifacts: Unsolved: cost (scalar 3614 ns, 72.5x, hash-only control; 6991 ns, 139.4x, Perlin control; 1239 ns, 23.8x, global axis) and straight spoke trunks in plan view. Final scans show 0 true jumps (elevation worst 0.000, mask worst 0.092). The scalar_vs_perlin value is for hash-only control, while the listed params and terrain images use Perlin control (139.4x).
catchment-rivers.node_shape: Feature Scale, K Upstream Rows, Area Exponent, Hillslope, Trunk Cell Size, Control, Output {Elevation, LogArea, Channel}.
catchment-rivers.port_notes: Walker identity checked on the hash lattice: 900 sites, 0 mismatches, K=16, largest area 97. Window is 4 rows x 5 sites centred per row in sheared coordinates. The local frame needed an ownership metric d + 0.5*overshoot, a fade at the window limit, a fade at the side flip past segment ends, and sinks owning no frame. Before these fixes the scan found 12 true jumps, worst 1.67; after them, 0. Height evaluates area on all 20 candidates, which is the cost. K barely changes the look, so try K=2 in a port.

critic.notes: Seed 7 at window 16 and seed 42 at window 48 confirm: the hillshaded elevation is the most convincing eroded-mountain texture in the family, but the trunk valleys are straight segments meeting at star hubs, obvious at every seed and dominant at the wide view. The relief at seed 7 is a dense spiky range rather than a readable drainage basin. The channel mask is poor (thick straight trunks over speckle). 3D is extruded laminae. The reported 72.5x is the hash-control figure; the listed params use Perlin control and cost 145x Perlin scalar, which the prototyper did disclose in artifacts but the headline number hides. The K sweep being indistinguishable, plus the DrainageFrame discovery reaching a similar look with no walkers, says the exact-area machinery is not what makes this look good. Worth keeping as a showcase heightmap example; not worth a node of its own.

tournament.notes: Seed 7 window 16 and seed 42 window 48 rendered. master.one_liner: Exact upstream drainage area per point at O(K) cost, using a Scheidegger river lattice whose catchment boundaries are two backward walkers. The network model is known hydrology (from memory); the pointwise area trick and the node are not something I recognise.
master.look: Eroded badland or mountain-flank drainage: tributaries merge into progressively wider channels, and the area output reads as real river bodies. Good for valley carving, river masks, wetness and sediment masks, and tree or biome placement. Fractal detail across scales comes from the network itself (Hack scaling), so one fine lattice covers many stream orders without octaves.
master.algorithm:
Lattice: rows r along the flow axis, sites e across it, at position X(e,r)=e-0.5*r plus hash jitter (world scale RX across, RY along). One hash bit d(e,r) in {0,1}. Each site flows to (e+d, r+1). The map is monotone, so channels can merge but never cross, and the upstream set of any site at any earlier row is a single interval.
Area: L=e-1; R=e; area=R-L; for m=1..K { L-=d(L,r-m); R-=d(R,r-m); area+=R-L }. The two walkers are the dual tree, meaning the catchment divides. R-L can never go negative and they coalesce at the source, so no masks are needed.
Surface: for each candidate segment (rows r-2..r+2, sites e0-2..e0+2 in the test; try 3x4 in the port), project to get t and dist. Lerp log(area) along the segment so a tributary and its trunk share the same value at the junction node. z=Zc*area^-theta + Tilt*(rows to outlet). height=min over candidates of z + S*dist. This lower envelope has no local pits, unlike FBm.
Outputs: Elevation, Channel mask with width ~ sqrt(area), log Area, Distance to divide (the same search on dual segments).
Pinnate mode: fold the row coordinate with a triangle wave of period T and add a trunk valley at the fold.
master.why_new: Flow accumulation normally needs a whole-grid simulation. Here it is a pure function of position, and it is exact whenever K reaches the divide. Nothing on the contact sheet or in a graph can report how much terrain drains through a point.
master.simd_plan: Branch free: masks for nearest-segment tracking, then fixed K-loop walkers on the winning segment's endpoints, 2 hashes per walker row. Adjacent sites share dual walkers, so a row of n sites needs n+1 walkers if areas are needed for all candidates. Estimate, not measured: nearest search about 2x CellularDistance 2D, K=32 about 128 hashes, total 40-70 ns, about 40-60x Perlin and 10-15x CellularDistance. 3D has no interval property with a 2D lateral: use crossfaded 2D laminae over z (2x cost). 4D does not tile, because the fold and flow axis are not periodic on the torus; native tiling needs hash modulo per axis.
master.continuity: Lower envelope of continuous functions is C0 if the candidate window is large enough. The test still showed outlier per-pixel jumps (max 6.8 vs p99.9 2.6, cause not identified; suspect window truncation or clamped rows).
master.params: Flow Angle (float), Aspect RX/RY (float), K Upstream Rows (int), Area Exponent theta (hybrid), Hillslope S (hybrid), Tilt (hybrid), Channel Width (hybrid), Output (enum). A deliberate lateral drift bias on d can also be hybrid.
master.risks: TESTED in numpy on baked arrays, not as a hash-based pointwise node. Walker identity matched brute-force accumulation at all 172 sites checked (0 mismatches). The look is NOT yet solved: at Aspect 1 the result is long parallel vertical gullies with visible zigzag and seams at the fold. At Aspect 3 plus domain warp the area map looks like rivers, but the height output looks closer to warped marble than dendritic terrain. Strong axis bias needs warp or a local flow frame. Tune or switch to channel-mask output before judging. Area is truncated when K is below the distance to the divide.
master.cost_note: Estimate, not measured: nearest search about 2x CellularDistance 2D, K=32 about 128 hashes, total 40-70 ns, about 40-60x Perlin and 10-15x CellularDistance.

fern-fold.look: As specified (parallel trunks, no window): the prettiest individual branches in the family at close range, a meandering stem with tapered side branches and twigs, but it is obvious horizontal bands, and the wide panel is rows. A warp bends the rows into contour-like streamlines and they still read as rows. The Voronoi province layout gives separate sprigs with gaps, like scattered plants, not a connected network. Drainage layout (added here: folded tributaries grown off steepest-descent trunks in each segment's own frame): a connected network with long trunks and dense feathery tributaries, no axis. It reads as rivers at the close view, and as frost or lightning at 19 cells where tributary density gets high. At 77 cells it shows strong white and dark blotches from the width proxy. Relief: valley network with cliffy edges, and the most dramatic canyon in the set. 3D vol: a few parallel tube trunks with very thin sparse twigs; mostly empty.

fern-fold.range: Line output [-1,1], saturating. Carve test not normalised, min 0.183, max 1.738 at these params.
fern-fold.artifacts: c0ratio 4.07 is on the valley output; the line output reads 1.0-1.5 from probe saturation. Jump scanner: 0 true jumps (worst 0.012). Scalar 2688 ns drainage, 277 ns (5.47x) parallel. Unsolved: the cheap form has bands, and the bandless form costs the same as dendry.

Fading on the cell coordinate as the entry says held up.

critic.notes: I disagree with 'reads as rivers up close': at seed 7 the drainage layout reads as lightning or frost at every scale, with dense feathery side branches at a fixed angle, and at seed 42 window 48 it is a dense bright scribble. notes: LICENCE: implement from the paper. The reference code is GPL-3.0 and must not be fetched.
Anything that modulates a segment must be a property of the segment, not of the sample's cell: a sample-window normalisation gave 17 true jumps.

Exact ties are common (a child nearest to the point two parent segments share), and SIMD lanes differ in which window sees a child, so visit parents lowest cell first and keep positions exact (hash bits times Epsilon in 1/256ths). Without that a straddle scan found 1556 jumps in 25.6M pairs; fnlab seams found none.

master.one_liner: Dendritic river, frost, lightning and vein networks from recursive coordinate folding: one hash per level, no lattice window, and a fade rule that keeps every seam continuous.
master.look: Branching trees with real width hierarchy: a meandering stem with tapered side branches at every level. It reads as a river network from the air, a frost fern, lightning, roots or leaf veins. Subtracted from fBm it gives gully-dissected terrain.
master.algorithm: Trunks: c=round(y/S); v=y-c*S; u=x+11.3*c; id=hash(c); edge=|y-c*S|/(S/2); mask=smoothstep(0.98,0.8,edge); v+=meander*noise1D(u,c); line=bump(|v|/w)*mask. For each level k in a fixed loop: side=(v>=0); vv=|v|; a=vv/sin(theta) (distance along the branch); ub=u+vv*cot(theta) (constant along a branch heading upstream); ci=round(ub/s); cellb=ub/s-ci (the seam is exactly at +-0.5); h=hash(ci, id+side+13k, seed+100k); gate=r0<keep; L=s*(lenMin+lenVar*r3); u0=(ci+0.55*(r1-0.5))*s; b=(ub-u0)*sin(theta)+bend*(r4-0.5)/s*a*a; al=min(a,L); dl=hypot(b,a-al[,cross axes]); parent=mask*smoothstep(0.5,0.36,|cellb|)*gate; line=max(line,bump(dl/(w*wr*(1-0.65*al/L)))*parent); mask=parent*smoothstep(L,0.75*L,a); then u=-a; v=b; id=h; w*=wr; s*=ratio. In 3D/4D the unused axes are cross axes: include them in dl and swap (v,cross)=(cross,b) each level so branch planes alternate. Valley output: sum over levels of depth_k*bump(dl/(carve*w_k))^2*parent, for subtracting from a terrain.
master.why_new: No existing node makes a tree: Ridged and F2-F1 give closed nets with no hierarchy. Branch order comes directly from the level index, so width needs no upstream-area pass. Dendry reports about 10 s for 512x512 on a quad core (about 38 us per sample wall clock), against an estimated 10 ns here.
master.simd_plan: Fixed loop over Levels with masks and Select only; the side bit goes into the hash as an int. No window, so cost barely depends on dimension. Estimates from handbook per-feature costs, not measured: 5 levels at 6-10 ns in 2D (6-9x Perlin, 2x CellularDistance), 7-11 ns in 3D (under 1x CellularDistance), 8-12 ns in 4D (0.25x CellularDistance). Generic GenT code works because extra axes are only cross distance.
master.continuity: C0 by construction. Every seam fades to zero on the cell coordinate before jitter and bend. Where the side flips (v=0), the parent line is at least as strong as any child, so max() hides the change. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps over 6 lines of 200k steps. Computing the fade on the bent b gave 14 real jumps, so that ordering matters.
master.params: Levels (int), Trunk Spacing, Branch Spacing, Spacing Ratio, Width, Width Ratio, Branch Length, Keep Probability, Output {Line, Valley}, Trunk Layout {Parallel, Provinces}. Hybrid-safe: Branch Angle, Width, Bend, Meander. Branch Spacing must stay constant because it sets cell indices.
master.risks: Parallel trunks read as bands. A Voronoi province layout (per-cell heading, fade by F2-F1) looked better in the prototype but adds a 3^D window. A line network is 1D, so 3D and 4D slices show only scattered dots (confirmed in a 3D slice), and a 4D torus tile will not resemble the 2D look. An elevation-consistent terrain output was tried and looked like herringbone, so only carving is proposed; carved valleys do not form hydrologically consistent drainage against the base height. The prototype used arbitrary tuning.
master.cost_note: Estimates from handbook per-feature costs, not measured: 5 levels at 6-10 ns in 2D (6-9x Perlin, 2x CellularDistance), 7-11 ns in 3D (under 1x CellularDistance), 8-12 ns in 4D (0.25x CellularDistance).

The province layout looks like fur patches. master.one_liner: Pointwise dendritic river and root networks: each lattice node picks one downstream neighbour with a hash bit, so a real branching tree emerges with no heights, sinks or global pass.
master.look:
Branching drainage trees with tributaries merging into wider trunks. Unlike anything on the contact sheet, whose line features are all closed cell walls or loops. Prototype K=4 grow 0.6 gives clear trunk and twig hierarchy. With fractal simplex warp (K=8, warp 0.7) the straight segments become convincing rivers. For river carving, roots, lightning, cracks with direction, vein networks, 3D root and cave systems.
[LatticeGraph (DrainageTree + BondNet), lattice-kernels] Drainage basins, roots, lightning, veins, mycelium; bonds give trusses, scaffolds, road or PCB nets. Prototyped: real dendritic merging with thicker trunks, all flowing one way; very unlike anything on the contact sheet. Hillshade of negated output carves valleys.
master.algorithm: Coalescing random walks (the Scheidegger river model; the model is from memory, not a consulted source). Brick lattice, rows j along the flow axis. Node position n(i,j) = (i + 0.5 + 0.5*(j&1) + J*(rx-0.5), j + 0.5 + J*(ry-0.5)). Child of (i,j) is in row j-1: column i+b for odd j, i-1+b for even j, b = one hash bit, optionally biased. Edge = segment n(i,j) to n(child). Field: min over window of segment distance d divided by width(Q). Window: rows cj-1..cj+2, columns ci-2..ci+2 (20 edges, as in the prototype, safe up to J=1 and cutoff 1 cell), or 3 rows by 4 columns (12 edges) if J<=0.5 and cutoff<=0.25. Discharge Q (optional depth K): count upstream nodes draining through a node with a row DP, m[r+1] = ((m[r]<<1) & ~B[r+1]) | (m[r] & B[r+1]) with parity adjust, Q = sum popcount(m[r]). B is a single 32-bit hash word holding the direction bits of 32 columns in a row. width = w0*(1 + grow*sqrt(lerp(Qa,Qb,t)-1)) with t the projection along the edge. Outputs: Distance, RiverMask, Order (log Q at the nearest edge). 3D: flow along one axis with 2 bits choosing among 4 children, giving tube networks. 4D: 3 bits, 8 children.
master.why_new: Rivers are the classic gap. Voxel Tools docs and a Godot voxel write-up both describe rivers as squared or absolute noise or Worley edges, which give closed loops with no tributaries and no flow. Dendry solves the tree pointwise but needs 9x9 points and a 7x7 lowest-neighbour pass per level plus control function evaluations (read in its code; the paper's own abstract reports about 10 s for a 512x512 grid on a quad core). It is also GPL-3.0. This keeps the tree topology with one bit per node and is cheap enough for SIMD. Graphs cannot express it: tree topology needs per-cell link information.
master.simd_plan: Fixed window, one hash per node, direction bit taken from the same hash. Segment distance is dot, clamp and one divide per edge, kept branch free with Min. Discharge uses the row-word trick so K rows need about K+window word hashes plus bit ops per node, popcount via SWAR, all integer lane ops. Scalar prototype K=0 with the 20-edge window: 4.4x perlin2, 2x its 5x5 worley2. Estimated AVX2: 2D 12 to 20 ns K=0, 25 to 35 ns K=8. 3D 50 to 80 ns (27 to 48 edges). Above the 5x Perlin guideline; justified as there is no cheap alternative for this topology.
master.continuity: Distance is C0 with medial-axis creases, like F1. Width interpolates along each edge, so RiverMask is C0 (measured c0ratio 8.0 at K=0, 6.8 at K=4 unwarped; 8.3 with warp). Direction bits never change output discontinuously because every edge is present in the window.
master.params: Feature Scale, Jitter, Direction Bias (hybrid), Width and Width Growth (hybrid), Discharge Depth K (int, loop count), Max Distance, Output enum.
master.risks:
Single global flow axis: rivers do not follow terrain downhill. Use DomainRotate, a warp, or a polar map, and carve the terrain with the mask rather than the reverse. Independent octaves cross each other (seen in the oct=2 prototype, a cross-hatch), so hierarchical tributaries need a parity-refined lattice, which is unsolved here. A 2D slice of the 3D or 4D form shows dashes and dots, and hypertorus tiling is not meaningful; tile by wrapping the lattice instead. Discharge width steps visibly if K is small. The 5x Perlin budget is exceeded.
[LatticeGraph (DrainageTree + BondNet), lattice-kernels] Lattice angles show at low jitter: segments look zig-zag (prototype visible). Fix with Jitter about 0.45 or a small warp. True flow accumulation is not available pointwise, so very long trunks do not keep thickening; octave stacking at 2x scale helps. No consistent downhill height in the output.
master.cost_note: Estimated AVX2: 2D 12 to 20 ns K=0, 25 to 35 ns K=8. 3D 50 to 80 ns (27 to 48 edges).
master.variant_notes: Scheidegger coalescing walks: one hash bit per node with discharge by row word DP. Triangular-lattice form from LatticeGraph. Single global flow axis.

master.one_liner: Pointwise depression filling: the lake level at p is the min over a fan of rays of the max of the source along each ray, so basins fill to their spill point and output either flooded terrain, lake depth or a flat-floor mask.
master.look: Smooth terrain with flat water surfaces / playas / alluvial floors in every closed depression, each at its own correct spill height; the Depth output is a clean lake mask. Prototyped: SpillSmooth / SpillSmoothMask (12 dirs x 6 samples on a 1-octave base). With a multi-octave source the ray fan undersamples and prints directional ridges inside lakes (terrain_round2 Spill8/Spill16), so the intended use is a low-frequency basin source plus detail added afterwards, or more samples.
master.algorithm: h = S(p). For D fixed directions (D=8..16 on the unit circle in 2D; in 3D the 26 neighbour directions or a 2-ring icosahedral set) and N samples per ray at distances t_k = R*k/N: m_d = max_k S(p + t_k*dir_d) (start m_d = h). L = min_d m_d (or a smooth-min with temperature param to hide fan faceting). Outputs: Flooded = max(h, L); Depth = L - h (water depth / sediment thickness mask); Fill Fraction = smoothstep(0, Blend, L - h). Interpretation: a point is under water if every escape route within radius R must climb above its height; it is exact for depressions narrower than R with a spill pass in a sampled direction, and conservative otherwise. Cheaper lattice variant (not prototyped): per coarse cell, spill = min over the 8 neighbour-boundary midpoints of S, blended across cells with a partition of unity; fills only cell-sized basins but costs 9 evals.
master.why_new: Depression filling (Priority-Flood) is the textbook global operation nobody can do in a pointwise graph; Min/Max/Remap cannot know where the spill point is. A radius-limited ray estimate turns it into a fixed-cost, stateless node. Flat-floored basins at varying heights are a dominant landform cue (lakes, salt flats, valley fill, glacial tarns) and are absent from the contact sheet.
master.simd_plan: D*N + 1 source evaluations with constant loop counts, running Max/Min per lane, direction table precomputed when params are set; smooth-min via Exp if enabled. 2D at 12x6 = 73 evals -> ~75x source (about 80 ns with Perlin); 3D with 26 directions x 4 samples = 105 evals; 4D: 80 directions x 3 is the ceiling. Honest cost tier: 'use on a cheap basin source'.
master.continuity: C0: max and min over a fixed set of continuous functions. Measured c0ratio 7.99-8.00. Per-lane random fan rotation (tried) breaks it and must not be used; rotate the fan by a low-frequency continuous angle instead if faceting matters.
master.params: Source, Radius (hybrid), Directions (int enum 8/12/16), Samples per ray (int), Output enum {Flooded, Depth, Fill Fraction}, Smooth Min temperature, Blend.
master.risks: Angular and radial aliasing: polygonal lake outlines and faint ridges inside lakes when the source has detail finer than the sample spacing. Basins wider than Radius are only partially filled (leaves a ring of water, which can look like a lakeshore terrace, sometimes acceptable). Expensive; a lattice-based single-level variant is the fallback.
master.cost_note: 2D at 12x6 = 73 evals -> ~75x source (about 80 ns with Perlin); 3D with 26 directions x 4 samples = 105 evals; 4D: 80 directions x 3 is the ceiling.
